ShortDescription.Value: Custom zones that grow only the buildings you choose, from any theme, region pack or custom asset.

Publish.LongDescription:
A Cities: Skylines II mod in the spirit of Building Themes from the original Cities: Skylines. Create zones with custom rules, choose exactly which buildings grow in each, and paint them with normal zoning tools.
Tired of micromanaging 20 different zone types or plopping buildings by hand to get a range of buildings and realistic cities? Want to allow both residential and commercial buildings in the same zone? Want to finely control building heights? Then this mod is for you. It adds the ability to easily zone for any available building using a set of basic zoning rules, and then customize the buildings chosen to your heart's content.
# Features - **Custom zones**: each zone is based on a game zone (its demand, services and toolbar icon) and can be customized however you would like. - **Zoning rules**: restrict what grows by its use, theme or region pack, height, lot width and depth, side setbacks, and parking. - **Per-building control**: include or exclude any building by hand, with thumbnails and filters. - **All sources**: vanilla, DLC, region packs and custom assets are all supported. Custom assets are grouped by the asset pack they came from. - **Saves that survive without the mod**: every save, autosaves included, is written with game zones in place of custom zones, so a city loads safely even if the mod is removed, broken by a game update, or no longer maintained. Your custom zones come back on load while the mod is installed. - **Safe retirement and uninstall**: retiring a custom zone rezones it back to game zones in the open city, with each building returned to its own game zone and empty lots given the zone's base zone. Retired zones can be restored or deleted. "Prepare for uninstall" (in Options) does this for every custom zone in a city, to make the change permanent. - **Translations**: 12 languages, machine translated; corrections welcome.
# Use 1. Open the panel with the zoning button in the top-left toolbar, or press Shift+Z (rebindable in Options). 2. Create a zone, set its rules, review the buildings, and Apply. 3. Paint the zone from the "Real Zoning" tab of the zoning toolbar.
Zones are saved in ModsData\RealZoningBuildingThemes\zones.json and shared by all your cities. Where you paint them is saved with each city.
# Requirements - **Unified Icon Library**: required for the zone type icons.
# Compatibility - **Plop the Growables**: supported. Its plopped buildings are left alone, and its despawn setting is honored. - **Placemaker**: supported. Buildings that Outgrow joins and bends count as the design they were made from, so they stay in custom zones that allow that design. - **Zone Organizer**: supported. Custom zones stay in a separate tab. - **Platter**: mostly works. Custom zones can be painted on parcels created by Platter and the appropriate buildings will grow; however, Platter's building counts will show 0 for each configuration.
# Uninstalling Cities saved with version 1.0.2 or later load safely without the mod: custom-zoned areas come back as game zones, with every building on its own game zone, so nothing is demolished. Empty lots there grow buildings of the zone's base zone. Saving the city without the mod makes that permanent; with the mod installed again before that, the custom zones come back.
Cities last saved with an earlier version are not protected until they are saved once with 1.0.2 or later. To make a city's game zones permanent while the mod is installed, go to Options > Real Zoning & Building Themes and press **Prepare for uninstall**, then save.
Deleting a zone hides it but keeps it registered, so other cities that use it still load safely.
# Credits and license Code was written by Claude Opus 5.5, with extensive human oversight in every step in the process. Results have been tested on multiple heavily-modded cities without issue.
Includes code adapted from Plop the Growables by algernon (Apache 2.0) and Custom Zones by dvovo (MIT). Inspired by Building Themes by boformer.
